expected: Feasible on the first try: accuracy ~0.752-0.758 and time ~7-9 s. Between the two repeats, accuracy spread <= 0.3 pp and time spread <= 0.2 s. If accuracy is < 0.753, the next epoch idea sets feasibility.
description: Replace the template recipe in submissions/arena/ with an airbench96-style net. Layers: frozen 2x2 patch-whitening conv (eigendecomposition computed in prepare), then three blocks of 3 convs with widths 128/384/576, BN, GELU, maxpool, then a scaled linear head with 100 outputs. Use dirac init on block convs. Train with Nesterov SGD using airbench96 lr, wd and momentum, label smoothing 0.2, Lookahead, and a linear warmup/decay schedule. Hold the full uint8 dataset on the GPU and do flip (alternating), translate 4 and cutout 12 on the GPU. Batch 1024, 8.5 epochs, bf16, channels_last, no TTA. torch.compile and warmup run in build on synthetic data; eval uses a separate path that is legal for any B. Run it twice in a row to measure the noise floor.

expected: Accuracy rises ~0.6-1.2 pp over 8.5 epochs, to ~0.762-0.768. Time rises roughly linearly, ~+1.3-1.6 s over the 8.5-epoch run. The slope and intercept tell us where the 0.753 crossing is.
description: On the H1.1.1 recipe, change only the epoch count to 10 (schedule rescaled to match). This secures a feasible anchor and gives one point for the accuracy-vs-epoch slope.

expected: Accuracy drops ~0.8-1.5 pp below 8.5 epochs, to ~0.740-0.747 (infeasible). Time is ~1.2 s lower. A smooth monotone curve confirms H1.1.2; a sharp cliff refutes the smooth-interpolation part.
description: On the H1.1.1 recipe, change only the epoch count to 7 (schedule rescaled). This is the lower point of the sweep, used to interpolate the cheapest feasible epoch count.
note: E001 is 2.3 pp below the edge at 8.5 ep; a 7-epoch point far below the edge does not help locate the crossing

expected: Time falls 5-12% (~0.4-1.0 s) and accuracy changes by < 0.3 pp. If the gain is under 3%, launch overhead is not the bottleneck.
description: On the best feasible airbench96 recipe, change only the compile setting: default compile becomes torch.compile(mode='max-autotune'), with CUDA-graph capture of the fixed-shape train step done in build. Handle the last partial batch by dropping it or padding it to a fixed shape. Eval stays on a separate non-graphed dynamic path; check B in {1, 7, 1024} under 5 s.

expected: In the under-fitting regime, accuracy rises +0.3-0.8 pp at equal time. If the gain is >= 0.4 pp, an ~0.5-epoch cut becomes possible later. If accuracy falls, the airbench96 defaults are already well regularized for 100 classes.
description: At the 8.5-epoch airbench96 recipe, change only the regularization: remove cutout and lower label smoothing from 0.2 to 0.1. Translate and flip stay as they are.

expected: Random flip lowers 3-seed accuracy by ~0.2-0.5 pp at the same time. A drop >= 0.3 pp supports H4.3.1; a drop within noise (< 0.2 pp) refutes it for this budget.
description: At the 8.5-epoch airbench96 recipe (which uses alternating flip), change only the flip to standard random per-image flip. This is the reverse ablation, testing whether alternating flip contributes on CIFAR-100.

expected: Time falls ~0.05-0.2 s and accuracy changes by < 0.3 pp. A cheap, nearly free win if prepare is a visible share of the score.
description: On the best feasible recipe, change only the input to the whitening eigendecomposition: compute it on 5,000 randomly chosen training images (patches drawn from them) instead of all 50,000. Everything else stays fixed.

expected: FLOPs per epoch fall ~45%, but accuracy per epoch drops ~1.5-2.5 pp. Predicted accuracy at 10 epochs is ~0.745-0.755 at a time ~20-30% below the wide net at 8.5 epochs. If it is feasible, that is a large win; if not, it maps the width trade-off.
description: Explore: change only the widths to 128/256/384 (same 3-convs-per-block layout) and set epochs to 10 to compensate for the lower capacity. Compare it with the best feasible 128/384/576 run.

expected: Early epochs cost about 44% fewer FLOPs, so total time drops about 10-18% (about 0.8-1.4 s at ~8 s). Accuracy changes by -0.2 to -0.7 pp. If the drop is <= 0.3 pp, H3.2.1 is supported and some of the saved time can go into extra epochs. A drop > 0.6 pp, or a recompile stall showing up in timed train, refutes it for this budget.
description: Explore. Start from the 8.5-epoch airbench96 recipe (I001) and change only the training resolution schedule. For the first 50% of steps, each augmented 32 px batch is downsampled to 24x24 with F.interpolate (bilinear, antialias=False) after flip, translate and cutout. The remaining steps stay at 32 px. The whitening conv and the rest of the net are unchanged; the 2x2 patch whitening and maxpools work at 24 px, giving 3x3 final maps before the global pool. Keep the LR schedule tied to step count, not resolution. In build, compile and warm up both input shapes (24 and 32 px) on synthetic data so no recompile happens in timed train. Eval stays at 32 px only.
note: ideate: Rewritten as a new idea on the current best recipe (E004, 10 epochs, no cutout, max-autotune + CUDA graphs with both shapes captured). The old version started from the infeasible 8.5-epoch I001 recipe with cutout, so the comparison would no longer reflect the main line.

expected: Time ~6.5-7.5 s (about 15-25% below 8.94 s). Accuracy ~0.740-0.755. If it reaches >= 0.753, H1.2.1 is supported and the narrow-and-longer branch becomes the main line. If accuracy is < 0.745, then width buys more than epochs on CIFAR-100 (consistent with C0014), so H1.2 loses confidence.
description: Explore. Rewrite of I008 onto the current best recipe. Start from E004 (no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, max-autotune + CUDA graph). Change only the widths, from 128/384/576 to 128/256/384 (same 3 convs per block), and set the epochs to 12 (schedule rescaled) to make up for the lower capacity. Estimated conv FLOPs per epoch are ~0.62x of the wide net.

expected: Time falls 10-18% (~0.9-1.5 s, to ~7.5-8.0 s). Accuracy drops 0.2-0.8 pp. A drop of <= 0.3 pp supports H3.2.1 and gives a recipe that can afford +1 epoch while still being faster. A drop of > 0.6 pp, or recompile stalls inside the timed train, refutes it.
description: Explore. Rewrite of I009 onto the current best recipe. Start from E004 (10 epochs, no cutout). Change only the resolution schedule: for the first 50% of steps, downsample each augmented batch to 24x24 (F.interpolate, bilinear, antialias=False) after flip and translate. The remaining steps run at 32 px. Keep the LR schedule tied to step count. Compile and capture CUDA graphs for both input shapes on synthetic data in build so no recompile lands in timed train. Eval stays at 32 px.
note: committee: most informative (outside the evidence), +1 priority

expected: Time about 8.2-8.35 s (E008 runs at 0.75 s/epoch at 10 epochs, so 11 epochs is about 8.27 s). That is 7-8% below E004's 8.94 s. Accuracy +0.4 to +0.8 pp over E008's 0.7495, to about 0.753-0.757. If it is feasible this becomes the new best. If accuracy lands at 0.750-0.753, the per-epoch slope near 10-11 epochs is flatter than 0.87 pp/epoch (W4's saturation view, not W2's linear one), and the next step is 11.5 epochs or a smaller low-res fraction rather than more epochs.
description: Exploit: combine the near-miss E008 with more epochs. Start from E008, commit cd99006: E004 recipe, 50% of steps at 24 px using bilinear F.interpolate with antialias=False, both shapes compiled and CUDA-graphed in build. Change only the epoch count, from 10 to 11, with the LR schedule rescaled to the new step count so it still anneals fully. First confirm in the commit that E004 and E008 really ran 10 epochs. Timing says they did (E004 8.94 s is about E003's 10-epoch 9.01 s minus cutout), even though E004's description says 8.5.

expected: Accuracy +0.2 to +0.6 pp over E004's 0.7550, to about 0.757-0.761. Time unchanged within noise (±0.05 s). A gain of 0.4 pp or more banks enough margin to cut about 0.5 epoch (about 0.45 s) in a follow-up. A drop of 0.3 pp or more means translation is the one regularizer worth keeping (supports W4), and translate stays at 4.
description: Exploit and committee crux: on the E004 recipe (10 epochs, no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, max-autotune plus CUDA graph), change only the random-translate amplitude from 4 px to 2 px. Everything else, including the epoch count, stays fixed. W4 claims translate helps, but every run so far used translate 4, so this tests whether translate 4 still over-regularizes a net that under-fits at 10 epochs, as cutout and LS 0.2 did.

expected: Time about 7.7-8.0 s: at 10 epochs E007 got 0.70x the time from 0.57x the FLOPs, so 0.72x FLOPs gives about 0.80x per epoch, times 11 epochs. Accuracy about 0.749-0.756. If it is feasible, it is about 11-14% faster than E004, and block-3 width turns out to be the binding capacity (the E009 ceiling came from narrowing block 3). If accuracy is below 0.749, the width trade-off loses on CIFAR-100 at this budget, and H1.2 should be closed in favour of resolution and epoch levers.
description: Explore: narrow only the middle block. Starting from E004, change the widths from 128/384/576 to 128/256/576, keeping 3 convs per block, and set epochs to 11 with the schedule rescaled. Block 2 at 16x16 is the largest FLOP share (about 0.79 of 1.6 GMACs). Block 3's width is the likeliest source of the capacity the 100-class head needs, and E007/E009 cut both blocks. Estimated conv FLOPs per epoch are about 0.72x those of the wide net.

expected: Accuracy +0.1 to +0.4 pp over E008's 0.7495, to about 0.751-0.754. Time +0.0 to +0.1 s over 7.52 s. A gain of 0.25 pp or more means part of the resize penalty is aliasing, not lost resolution, and the fix carries into the 11-epoch resize line. A gain under 0.15 pp (noise) refutes the aliasing mechanism, and the cost of resizing is all resolution.
description: Mechanism test from D003 (C0029/C0031: aliasing from non-antialiased bilinear downsampling, which mismatches the 32 px-fit frozen whitening filters). On E008 (10 epochs, 50% at 24 px), change only the downsampling to F.interpolate(mode='bilinear', antialias=True), done inside the compiled and graphed step. Check in build that both shapes still capture without a recompile in timed train.

expected: Accuracy change -0.3 to +0.4 pp (direction uncertain); time unchanged. A gain of 0.3 pp or more frees margin to cut epochs. A loss of 0.3 pp or more puts the optimum smoothing between 0.05 and 0.1 and closes the smoothing branch.
description: On the E004 recipe, change only the label smoothing, from 0.1 to 0.0. This tests whether the leftover smoothing still over-regularizes at 10 epochs on 100 classes, or whether its calibration benefit outweighs that.

expected: Steps go from about 49 to 65 per epoch. Time rises 4-10%, to about 9.3-9.8 s. Accuracy +0.2 to +0.7 pp. The run is worth following up only if the gain is above about 0.9 pp per added second, which beats buying epochs. If the gain is under 0.3 pp, the regime is sample-limited, and larger batches (1536) for throughput become the next test.
description: Explore whether progress is limited by steps or by samples. On E004, change only the batch size, from 1024 to 768, at equal epochs. Under linear scaling, scale the per-step LR by 768/1024, keep wd per sample as airbench defines it, and tie the schedule to the new step count. Recapture the CUDA graph for the new shape in build and handle the last partial batch the same way as now.

expected: The main net's backward passes are halved per raw epoch, but the proxy forward and backward adds about 15-20%. Expected time about 8.0-8.8 s at matched main steps, and accuracy -0.3 to -1.0 pp relative to E004 (hard examples are noisy for 100 classes in an under-fitting regime). Likely infeasible, which would refute H3.1.1 and close H3.1. Feasible and under 8.0 s would be a surprise, worth expanding.
description: One decisive test, given that C0015/C0018 contradict it. On E004, add airbench96_faster-style proxy filtering: a 32/64/64 proxy net trained alongside, scoring each 2048-image superbatch, with the main net taking an SGD step only on the top-50% by loss. Main-net epochs are counted in seen-by-main samples, and the main-net step count matches E004. Compile and graph the proxy and the main steps in build.
note: committee: most informative (outside the evidence), +1 priority

expected: Accuracy +0.2 to +0.45 pp over E012's 0.7567, to about 0.759-0.761. Time unchanged within noise (7.70 ± 0.05 s), so this is not an improvement in time by itself. A gain of 0.25 pp or more confirms translate 2 as the new default and makes the resize combo (next idea) likely feasible. A gain under 0.15 pp means the narrowed net needs translate more than the wide net did, i.e. a width × regularization interaction, and the resize combo should get +1 epoch instead.
description: Exploit, building margin on the incumbent. Start from E012 (commit 6d40ead: 128/256/576, 3 convs per block, 11 epochs, no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, max-autotune + CUDA graph). Change only the random-translate amplitude from 4 px to 2 px (reflect padding, same as E011). Everything else, including the epoch count, stays fixed. On the wide net at 10 epochs, E011 showed translate 2 gave +0.35 pp. This checks whether the gain carries over to the block-2-narrowed net, and banks margin for the resize and epoch-cut follow-ups.
note: Already done: E012 (tip, 6d40ead) was built on E011 and already uses translate 2; there is no translate-4 incumbent to change

expected: Accuracy about 0.753-0.757 (+0.25 to +0.5 pp over E013). Time about 6.30-6.35 s, unchanged from E013. If accuracy is >= 0.753, this is a new best: about 18% faster than E012's 7.70 s. If it lands at 0.750-0.753, run the same recipe at 12 epochs next (~6.9 s).
description: Exploit by combining near-misses. Start from E013 (commit b0eba3b: E012 net, 128/256/576 at 11 epochs, first 50% of steps at 24 px via bilinear F.interpolate with antialias=True, both shapes compiled and graphed in build; 0.7510 at 6.32 s). Change only the translate amplitude, from 4 px to 2 px, in both phases. Rationale: E013 was about 0.2-0.25 pp short. Translate 2 was worth +0.35 pp on the wide net (E011). C0025 also says augmentation should be weaker at low resolution, and 4 px at 24 px is relatively ~5.3 px. One change, two supporting mechanisms.
note: Already done: E013 (b0eba3b) was built on E012 and already used translate 2; I020's change is a no-op

expected: Time about 6.85-6.95 s (+0.57 s/epoch). Accuracy +0.25 to +0.5 pp over 0.7510, to about 0.753-0.756. Feasible would beat E012 by about 10%. A gain under 0.2 pp would mean this net with resize is near its ceiling (H5.1), so more epochs are a poor lever and the margin has to come from regularization (translate 2).
description: Exploit fallback that buys accuracy with epochs instead of regularization. Start from E013 (128/256/576, 50% of steps at 24 px with antialias, translate 4). Change only the epoch count, from 11 to 12, with the LR schedule rescaled to the new step count so it still anneals fully. This measures the per-epoch slope of the narrowed net with resize near 75%, which E010's 0.31 pp/epoch flattening left open.

expected: Time about 6.4-6.6 s (the 28 px third costs ~0.85x). Accuracy about 0.752-0.755 (a loss of 0.15-0.45 pp vs E012). Supports H3.2.3 if the loss per second saved is < 0.3 pp/s, vs ~0.4 pp/s for the 50%-at-24 schedule; refutes it if the loss is >= 0.4 pp/s.
description: Explore a gentler resolution curriculum. On E012 (128/256/576, 11 epochs, translate 4), replace the full-resolution schedule with a 24/28/32 px curriculum in thirds of steps. Downsample the augmented batch with bilinear F.interpolate (antialias=True), with the LR schedule tied to step count. Compile and CUDA-graph all three shapes on synthetic data in build, and check that no recompile lands in timed train. Compare it with E013's 50%-at-24 px (0.41 pp lost per second saved).

expected: Time about 6.9-7.2 s (-7 to -10%). Accuracy -0.1 to -0.5 pp, to about 0.752-0.756. Feasible supports the 'cut early blocks, keep block 3' version of H1.2 and becomes a new best. A loss of 0.5 pp or more (infeasible) means the low-level features are binding, which closes width cuts outside block 2.
description: Explore the remaining cheap width axis. Per the FLOP accounting, after narrowing block 2, block 1 (128 ch at 32x32, ~0.45 GMACs) is about 35% of E012's conv FLOPs. On E012 (11 epochs, translate 4), change only the widths from 128/256/576 to 96/256/576, keeping 3 convs per block and the whitening output feeding block 1. E012 suggests that block-3 width carries the capacity 100 classes need, and that early-block width is cheap to cut.

expected: Time -3 to -6% (7.70 to about 7.30-7.45 s). Accuracy within ±0.2 pp of 0.7567. A cut under 2% means the optimizer is not a meaningful share of the ~19 ms step, which weakens H2.4 as the explanation for resize's 0.68x step cost.
description: Exploit throughput at equal math. On E012, move the Nesterov SGD + Lookahead update into compiled torch._foreach_* ops inside the CUDA-graph-captured train step. Read the per-step LR and Lookahead alpha from a precomputed GPU tensor table indexed by a GPU step counter, so there is no Python-side scalar update per step. Capture in build on synthetic data; prepare must still reset the parameters, the momentum buffers, the Lookahead slow weights and the step counter. The numerics must match the current update (verify the parameter delta in a short synthetic check).

expected: First-trial prepare falls from about 0.146 s to <= 0.08 s, so the 3-trial mean time drops by 0.02-0.03 s (7.70 to about 7.67-7.68 s). Accuracy unchanged. A drop under 0.01 s means the first-trial overhead is CUDA context or allocator work that this warm-up does not reach.
description: Free fixed-cost cleanup. On E012, in build, allocate and H2D-copy synthetic uint8 tensors of the exact real dataset shape ([50000,32,32,3] images, [50000] labels) through the same code path prepare uses (pinned staging, .cuda(), permute/normalize kernels), then free them. No real data is touched in build.
note: committee: most informative (outside the evidence), +1 priority

expected: Time about 7.0 s (7.70 x 10/11, -9%). Accuracy -0.15 to -0.6 pp, to about 0.751-0.755. If accuracy >= 0.753, this is a new best and the next step is 9.5 epochs. If it lands at 0.750-0.753, the slope below 11 epochs is steep (>= 0.4 pp/epoch, unlike the flat slope above it), so the next try is 10.5 epochs. If it falls below 0.750, epochs stay at 11 and margin has to come from elsewhere.
description: Exploit the flat per-epoch slope. E010 gave 0.31 pp/epoch and E017 gave 0.11 pp/epoch near 11 epochs, so cutting epochs may be the cheapest lever left. Start from the incumbent E012 (commit 6d40ead: 128/256/576, 3 convs per block, translate 2, no cutout, LS 0.1, alternating flip, max-autotune + CUDA graph, 11 epochs). Change only the epoch count, from 11 to 10, and rescale the LR/Lookahead schedule to the new step count so it still anneals fully. Report per-seed accuracy and the per-seed minimum. This measures this net's slope between 10 and 11 epochs: H1.1.4 asks the slope question of the wide net, and this asks it of the incumbent. If I023 (96/256/576) becomes the new tip first, apply the same 1-epoch cut to that tip instead.

expected: Time +0.3 to +0.45 s, to about 6.6-6.8 s. Accuracy +0.2 to +0.5 pp, to about 0.753-0.756. If feasible, this is ~12-14% faster than E012, which supports 'block-3 width is the binding capacity' and the H5 ceiling view: width raises the ceiling where epochs could not. A gain under 0.15 pp means block 3 is not binding either, and the resize line is capped near 0.752 for this family.
description: Combine near-misses: put block-3 capacity into the resize recipe. E012 suggests block-3 width is the capacity that 100 classes need. E013 and E017 sit 0.1-0.2 pp short, and extra epochs barely help there (E017 gave +0.11 pp/epoch). Start from E013 (commit b0eba3b: 128/256/576, 11 epochs, first 50% of steps at 24 px via bilinear antialias=True, translate 2, both shapes compiled and graphed in build; 0.7510 at 6.32 s). Change only block-3 width, from 576 to 704 (3 convs per block, head input widened to match). Block 3 runs at 8x8 (4x4 or 6x6 maps during the 24 px phase), so per-image conv MACs rise only ~0.2 G (~+15%).

expected: Time about -0.65 to -0.75 s, to about 6.95-7.05 s. Accuracy -0.2 to -0.35 pp, to about 0.753-0.755. Feasible means a new best, unless the epoch cut is cheaper per second. If the loss per second saved is < 0.3 pp/s, the resize cost is front-loaded or non-linear, so small fractions are efficient; ~0.4 pp/s confirms the linear line.
description: A smaller low-res fraction on the incumbent. All resize schedules so far land on ~0.4 pp lost per second saved (E008/E013/E018), and the cost seems to scale with the FLOPs removed. A 25% fraction uses that line where E012 has margin (0.37 pp). Start from E012 (11 epochs, translate 2). Change only the resolution schedule: the first 25% of steps run at 24 px (bilinear F.interpolate, antialias=True, after flip and translate, inside the compiled and graphed step); the rest run at 32 px. Capture both shapes in build and check that no recompile lands in timed train. This is the alternative to the epoch-cut idea for the same ~0.7 s: if both run, compare their pp lost per second saved.
note: Superseded: tip E023 already runs 50% of steps at 24 px (plus block3 704); a 25%-at-24px point on E012 projects to ~6.95-7.05 s, slower than the tip's 6.65 s

expected: Accuracy -0.15 to +0.3 pp (direction uncertain; without an EMA tail, a nonzero final LR may hurt). Time unchanged (7.70 +/- 0.05 s). A gain of 0.25 pp or more banks margin for the epoch cut and supports H4.5. A loss of 0.15 pp or more refutes H4.5.1 and keeps decay to 0.
description: Schedule constant tuned for long runs. On E012 (11 epochs, translate 2), change only the LR schedule end point: linear decay to 5% of peak instead of to 0, with warmup, Lookahead and everything else unchanged. Precompute the per-step LR the same way as now so the CUDA graph is unchanged. This is the decisive test of H4.5.1; the fulcrum CIFAR-10 champion uses an LR floor.
note: Already implemented: the airbench schedule in every run since E001 decays linearly to 0.07 of peak (not to 0), so the 'LR floor' is already in place

expected: Time -2 to -5%, to about 7.3-7.55 s (fewer, larger, better-utilized steps). Accuracy -0.05 to -0.35 pp, since there are ~33% fewer steps (~36 per epoch). If accuracy stays >= 0.753 and time falls >= 0.15 s, this is a new best and batch 1536 becomes the default. A time gain under 1.5% means the A100 is already saturated at 1024, which closes the batch axis.
description: Follow-up to E015, which showed the regime is sample-limited, not step-limited: going from batch 1024 to 768 left accuracy flat and cost +5% time. Test whether a larger batch buys throughput. On E012 (11 epochs, translate 2), change only the batch size, from 1024 to 1536. Keep the per-example LR and wd as airbench defines them (per-step LR x1.5), tie the schedule to the new step count, recapture the CUDA graph for the new shape in build, and handle the last partial batch the same way as now.

expected: Expected outcome: refuted. Accuracy -0.5 to +0.3 pp; time +3 to +8% (Newton-Schulz on 576x5184 matrices). A gain of 0.3 pp or more at a time cost under 4% would reopen the optimizer axis as an epoch-cut enabler. Otherwise close H4.2.
description: One decisive optimizer check. On E012 (11 epochs, translate 2), replace Nesterov SGD on the block conv filters (not the whitening layer, BN or head) with Muon in the airbench94_muon form: Newton-Schulz orthogonalized momentum, lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, nesterov. BN, biases and head stay on the current SGD with the current schedule. Lookahead stays as it is. Run Newton-Schulz in bf16 inside the compiled step and capture it in build. Prepare must reset the Muon momentum buffers.
note: committee: most informative (outside the evidence), +1 priority

expected: The ~2.3 ms/step of Muon overhead falls to ~0.6-1.0 ms/step, the NS matmul floor (a 704x6336 NS is ~0.25 ms). Time drops from 7.26 s to ~6.65-6.85 s. Accuracy is unchanged within noise at ~0.758-0.765. If time is <= 6.45 s it is a new best outright. Otherwise it is the base for the Muon epoch cut, where each epoch saved is worth ~0.6 s. If time stays > 7.0 s, NS compute rather than launch overhead dominates, and the next thing to try is fewer NS iterations.
description: Exploit: make Muon cheap at equal math. Start from E025 (commit 50d39d6: E024 tip plus Muon on the block conv filters, lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, nesterov; 0.7622 at 7.26 s). Change only how the Muon update is implemented, not what it computes. (a) Group the same-shape conv filters (block-2 conv2/conv3, block-3 conv2/conv3, and any others that match) and run Newton-Schulz on each stacked group as one batched bf16 bmm. (b) Put the whole Muon step (momentum update, nesterov blend, NS, renorm, param update) into the same compiled function as the fused foreach SGD+Lookahead update, inside the CUDA-graph-captured train step. Read the LR from the GPU step table. Momentum buffers stay persistent, are captured in build on synthetic data, and are zeroed in prepare. Check in a short synthetic test that the parameter delta matches E025's per-parameter loop to bf16 tolerance.

expected: Muon gave +0.78 pp, about 1.5 epochs' worth at ~0.52 pp/epoch near 10-11 ep (E020). Accuracy ~0.751-0.758, centred near 0.755. Time scales with steps: ~6.27 s from the E025 base, or ~5.7-5.9 s from a fused I032 base. Either is a new best if feasible (tip 6.45 s). If accuracy lands at 0.749-0.753, Muon's per-epoch slope is steeper than SGD's, and the follow-up is 10 epochs.
description: Exploit: spend Muon's accuracy gain on epochs. Start from the I032 result if it was kept as the Muon base, otherwise from E025 (commit 50d39d6). Change only the epoch count, from 11 to 9.5. Rescale the LR, Lookahead and Muon schedules to the new step count so they still anneal fully, and keep the 24 px phase at the first 50% of steps. Report per-seed accuracy. If the 3-seed mean margin over 0.753 is under 0.3 pp, rerun once and pool before promoting it (H1.1.3 rule).

expected: Time -2 to -4%, from 6.45 s to ~6.2-6.3 s, since fixed per-step overhead is spread over 25% fewer steps (~268 total). Accuracy -0.0 to -0.35 pp. The regime is sample-limited (E015, E024), but steps fall to ~24 per epoch, close to where step-limitation could show. Feasible is a new best, and the batch should then also carry over to the Muon line, where per-step NS cost is amortized the same way. A time gain under 1.5% means the GPU is saturated at 1536, which closes the batch axis.
description: Exploit throughput along the batch axis. On the tip E024 (128/256/704, 50% of steps at 24 px with antialias, translate 2, LS 0.1, alternating flip, batch 1536, fused foreach SGD+Lookahead, 11 epochs), change only the batch size, from 1536 to 2048. Hold the per-example LR and wd fixed (per-step LR x4/3), tie the warmup/decay and Lookahead schedule to the new step count, recapture the CUDA graphs for both resolutions in build, and handle the last partial batch the same way as now.

expected: Time unchanged (+/- 0.03 s). Accuracy -0.2 to +0.35 pp, direction uncertain. Training the whitening bias for 27% of an 11-epoch run may perturb the input distribution BN sees during the 24 px phase. Report per-seed accuracy.
